paragraphs.text: Only wool from the side of the springjack turned most often to the sun can be woven into kithkin battle standards. Jackherds record every movement of their woolly-jacks until shearing.
"I do not heal. Healing means that the pain has already been felt. To stop suffering, one must prevent the world's wounds altogether."
The flasks provide ballast, a means of steering, and—with a little luck—a way to deliver ward-spells to cohorts below.
Soul and bones, kithkin are woven into their clans. They fight fiercely and without self-interest.
The choke point was the plan, but devoted camaraderie was always her strategy.
There's nothing more unsettling than locking blades with something that looks just like you.
What self-indulgence tears down, discipline builds up again.
"There are all kinds of strengths, but if you have strength of soul, the others will follow." —Galanda Feudkiller
"Suddenly there stood a fortress protecting the clachan, its walls hewn of valor and mortared with honor." —*Clachan Tales*
"In my moment of death, I had a vision of the world, dark and unwelcoming. I wanted to hide in the deepest meander, but the light pulled me back."
"If one's life is blessed, solutions to all life's problems will appear at the right moment." —*The Book of Kith and Kin*

"Odum and Broadbark were the only beings mighty enough to challenge the giant Moran the Destroyer. Their battle lasted a hundred dawns, until Moran became so exhausted that he fell into namesleep. He awoke as Moran the Gardener." —*The Tale of Odum and Broadbark*
Ambidexterity is common among kithkin. The thoughtweft links the minds of the left- and right-handed, giving each the knack of the other.
His aim is as sure as a mosquito's sting, but with none of the warning.
"Should you take it in mind to ride a springjack, remember: there are easier ways to fly, and harder ways to break your skull." —Lann of Cloverdell
"If you need an example to lead others to the front lines, consider the precedent set."
"No matter how strong, an unarmed fighter is no more than a fool."
Merrow schools rarely form by design. They come together naturally as eager learners surround the wisest teachers.
"Tideshaping is more than creating a few new puddles."
His tales are as tall as he is, and only a giant's life is long enough to listen to them all.
Sometimes the weight of the world on your shoulders is a literal one.
Every story, even a faerie tale, comes to an end.
Only in dew from Oona herself is there clarity enough to see a victim's mind.
Gryffid scowled at the sky. A perfect day for the hunt tainted by clouds. He wished them gone. High above, the clouds looked down, scowled, and made a wish of their own.
Oona's song is like a twisted dinner chime. All the faeries return home, but it is Oona who feasts—on the stolen dreams and rumors they serve her.
You may as well try to swat a faerie —Flamekin expression meaning "that's impossible"
"The world above the waterline must be monitored—and, when necessary, adjusted."
Fragments of thought refract and multiply, surging in a geyser of dizzying insight.
"Ever seen a changeling fly into a lantern?" —Calydd, kithkin farmer
Masters of the arcane savor a delicious irony. Their study of deep and complex arcana leads to such a simple end: the ability to say merely yes or no.
"There is no secret that cannot be sold."
"Curse these merrows and their meddling! Since coming near the river, I can't so much as sneeze without being soaked." —Ashling the Pilgrim
"The reflection is true. It is you who are distorted and false."
Made from trout scales and crawfish whiskers, merrows' shimmering banners flash in the water like lightning.
Dreams are tempting because one is so powerful in them. Dreams are dangerous because that power is a lie.
In Lorwyn's brief evenings, the sun pauses at the horizon long enough for a certain species of violet to bloom with the fragrance of mischief.
"See the beauty in death: the clean white bones lying in the fertile soil and the brightly colored moonglove sprouting from the fell earth."
"What is drowned is not forgotten. I will fulfill my oath. Come back to me, my brethren, as I have come back for you."
A single festercreep isn't alone. It's already an infestation.
Many heroes' last sight is a grin at the other end of a rapier.
The Frogtossers thread feathers, bones, and trophies from past raids into their standards, believing they fuel the warren with the anger of its victims.
Maralen sent Veesa, Endry, and Iliona—the Vendilion clique—on the gravest of tasks.
Dark thoughts hatch and twist within the mind, straining to take wing.
Like the sun to a flower, the adoring gaze of the tribe is sustenance to an elf. To be shunned is to wither.
"Even without the spines, who would dare to touch it?" —Desmera, perfect of Wren's Run
"Rejoice, eyeblight. In your last hours above the earth, those who bury you will finally make you beautiful."
"Many believe it to be the manifestation of all that is vile about the boggarts. I believe it should be avoided—from upwind, if possible." —Cenn Deagan
A faerie is the offspring of Oona and mischief.
"And that's when it was discovered that boggarts have just half a brain." —*The Book of Other Folk*
"When Byoog reached down to pull up a bit of root for the stew, he didn't expect the root to pull back." —A tale of Auntie Wort
All boggarts have an auntie, but they don't all have a mum.
Even if giants bring nothing else on a journey, they bring attention.
"Now everyone knows what you are."
Giants share nothing but their fury.
The banner symbolizes the goodwill of the Brighthearth. Their emissaries bring the mastery of fire to other races.
Lorwyn's crust explodes with power when the greater elementals are born. The flamekin use the fallout as cover for forays into enemy territory.
"All beings carry the fire inside them. The challenge is to unleash it before they dwindle into oblivion." —Illulia, flamekin soulstoke
"One's plenty," observed the merrow. "Way too plenty," agreed the boggart.
They could agree on one thing only: one of them must die.
One voice is but a pebble to the rest of the world. A thousand voices at once is an avalanche.
"Flamekin death rites are elaborate and spectacular affairs. Their greatest fear is death in obscurity." —Tollek Worldwatcher, journal
More, more, more!
"Let the mountain's teeth pierce our oppressors."
"It is the nature of souls that they burn more brightly together than apart." —Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue
Disaster stalks with gaping jaws across unready lands.
A path vexed by the stingmoggie was probably the wrong path anyhow.
A spark to light the guttered heart.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
The flame of a warrior is never extinguished.
"Aren't there boggarts enough in Lorwyn? Couldn't it turn into a sheep? Or a sunflower?" —Olly of Goldmeadow
Treefolk and elves share a common interest in the forests, but really the elves just feel at home with the view from above.
Deep in a murmuring bosk, where the trees' memories span centuries, the simple banner of green and copper signifies an elder whose rings number more than a faerie's days.
Those who seek to escape her blades succeed only in dying on their stomachs.
The more pleasant an illusion's garb, the more indecent its form laid bare.
Gremil finally felt in touch with nature—and felt a need to share the experience with others.
As graceful as a deer leaping a stream and as deadly as the wolf waiting in ambush on the other side, elvish warriors are the eyes of the forest as well as its unsheathed claws.
"May you rise again, from seed to sapling to sentience."
"I pity them, never knowing the pleasures of a single familiar form, but at least they find a noble shape at times." —Desmera, perfect of Wren's Run
"In our hands, the natural world finds more beauty than nature alone could ever provide."
"My arrows will ever find you."
"Study the great spirits of our age and those of the past. Prune secrets from the branching traceries of our lineage." —Twila, Gilt-Leaf archdruid
"Eyeblights are easy to track. Just follow the imperfections."
Storms in Lorwyn don't patter on village rooftops, but rather drench the clachan in rays of amber light.
"After the Rising, a treefolk's mind is as limber and green as its limbs, and is at its most receptive to our teachings."
Growth has no limits.
Once a famed hunter and packmaster, now a renegade seeking his own path.
"Changes far greater than the turning of the leaves await us at season's end." —Colfenor, the Last Yew
A chorus of howls answers his call.
It's the flint that sparks a warrior's rage.
Some changelings born at Velis Vel never return, but their essence never leaves.
